    Infer cell-level circadian phase

    infer_cell_phase.Rd

    This function infers cell-level circadian phase from a gene-by-cell count matrix and a cell-level metadata table.

    infer_cell_phase(
  count,
  metadata,
  ZT_by,
  strata_by,
  seedgene = NULL,
  Species = c("auto", "human", "mouse"),
  n_grid = 60,
  n_iter_outer = 5,
  n_iter_seed = 3,
  Kappa = 5,
  p_mix = 0.85,
  Min_n = 200,
  setseed = 1,
  Verbose = TRUE
)

    Arguments

    count

    A gene-by-cell raw count matrix. count must be either a base R matrix or a sparse Matrix object, with genes in rows and cells in columns.

    metadata

    A data.frame containing cell-level metadata.

    ZT_by

    A character string specifying the column in metadata that contains sample-level Zeitgeber time in hours.

    strata_by

    A character string specifying the column in metadata used as the grouping variable for cell-level phase inference.

    seedgene

    An optional character vector of seed genes used for phase inference. If NULL, built-in default seed genes are used.

    Species

    Species used to select the built-in default seed-gene set when seedgene = NULL. One of "auto", "human", or "mouse".

    n_grid

    Number of discrete phase grid points used to approximate the circular latent phase space.

    n_iter_outer

    Number of outer iterations for phase inference.

    n_iter_seed

    Number of seed-gene fitting iterations within each outer iteration.

    Kappa

    Initial concentration parameter for the von Mises prior.

    p_mix

    Initial mixture weight between the structured von Mises component and the uniform background component.

    Min_n

    Minimum number of cells required in a stratum for stratum-level parameter updating.

    setseed

    Integer random seed used for reproducibility.

    Verbose

    Logical; if TRUE, progress messages are printed.

    Value

    A tibble with one row per cell. The returned columns include cell, ZT_input, stratum, theta_pred, ZT_pred, Rbar, and r_cell.

    Details

    The inferred cell phase may depend on the input analysis scope. Running infer_cell_phase() on a subset of cells is not guaranteed to produce identical results to running it on the full dataset and then subsetting, because seed-gene fitting and stratum-level prior updating are performed on the supplied data matrix.

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data("srb_example_data")

res_phase <- infer_cell_phase(
  count = srb_example_data$Count,
  metadata = srb_example_data$meta,
  ZT_by = "ZT",
  strata_by = "celltype",
  Species = "mouse",
  setseed = 1,
  Verbose = TRUE
)

head(res_phase)
} # }
